subject: Medisys evaluation: deployment & latency targets
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Wu <ben.wu@medisys.com>, Sarah Klein <sarah.k@medisys.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Medisys evaluation: deployment & latency targets

Thanks again for the time today — nice to meet you both. Quick recap and concrete next actions so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights
- Economic buyer: Sarah indicated procurement will own final sign-off; timeline target end of May.
- Primary decision criteria: 1) predictable p95/p99 latency, 2) per-token cost envelope, 3) hosting mode (Dedicated vs Private VPC), 4) SLA/uptime commitment and audit evidence.
- Latency target discussed: p95 under ~300ms for typical short-instruction workloads (~1k tokens/session). Sarah also asked about p99 expectations during bursts.
- Cost signal: goal is to stay below $2.50 per 1k tokens (inference-only compute) for steady-state batch.
- Security/procurement: Medisys will run a short RFI and ask for SOC 2 evidence, key rotation details, and data retention policies.

Attachments I'm including: redwood-sla-summary.pdf (short doc on SLA tiers & fallback), medisys-rfi-answers.xlsx (first-pass answers we drafted from the call).

Requested next steps
1) From Redwood: Aditya/Karthik to produce a concise Tech Note (1 page) showing expected p95/p99 for both Hosted and Dedicated with the workload assumptions, plus an estimated $/1M tokens cost for each hosting option. Please call out how prefix caching or batching assumptions change the numbers. (target: by Thu EOD PDT)
2) From Medisys: Ben to share the expected peak concurrency and an example request distribution (short vs long sequences) so we can tune numbers.
3) Procurement: Sarah to share the primary procurement contact and the RFI deadline (if available).

Open questions to resolve
- Would you prefer we model Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) or Private VPC for the primary deployment? We can provide both numbers but want to prioritize the one that matches your procurement path.
- Can you confirm SLO tolerance for failover windows (e.g., acceptable SLA credits / max failover time)?

If this looks right I'll flag the action items in the deal record and follow up with a short invite for a technical calibration call early next week.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai

Chloe — thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement: Sarah is the economic buyer but the procurement owner will be someone in vendor management (I should have that name Thursday). The RFI window is likely 2 weeks from when we receive the responses.
- Concurrency: We see steady traffic at ~40 concurrent requests during clinic hours, spiking to ~250 during batch jobs (these spikes last ~10-15 minutes). Typical request sizes: 80% are <300 tokens, 20% are 300-2k tokens.
- Deployment preference: if Dedicated reduces integration friction and gives predictable billing, that will be our preference — but procurement will evaluate cost delta versus Private VPC.

One ask: can Redwood provide a small short-lived sandbox (1–2 weeks) that routes to a Dedicated-like environment or a representative model so our engineers can run a latency profile? Even a managed demo with a small reserved capacity would work.

Happy to hop on a quick tech follow-up once you have the latency/cost estimates.

—Ben
Principal Product Manager, Medisys Health
ben.wu@medisys.com

Aditya / Karthik — looping you both for the technical deliverables. Ben gave us the concurrency and distribution above. Key asks: 

1) Please draft a one-page Tech Note that shows assumptions and projected p95/p99 for both Hosted (our low-friction hosted offering) and Dedicated (reserved capacity). Include two rows: steady-state (40 concurrency) and spike (250 concurrency, 10-15m). Call out whether KV/prefix caching is assumed (I think we should show with and without caching).
2) Cost estimate: show $ per 1M tokens for both modes and note quantization/instance assumptions. He gave a target of ~$2.50/1k tokens — highlight where we're within/outside that band.
3) Sandbox: can we provision a short-lived dedicated sandbox? If not, propose a low-cost hosted demonstration that replicates Dedicated latency for the short window. Ben prefers Dedicated-like behaviour.

Timeline: Chloe to send to Ben and Sarah by Thu EOD. If you need more data from them, ask now.

Thanks — Chlo

Ben / Sarah — thanks for the details and the RFI window heads-up. Quick responses and a proposed next step: 

1) Sandbox: We can provision a short-lived Dedicated sandbox (2x A100-equivalent instance) for a 10-day window. It will mimic a reserved capacity environment — cost will be covered by Redwood for the evaluation. If that works, let me know preferred start date and an approved list of IPs for VPC access.

2) Latency projections (high-level) — assumptions: model = redwood-llm-v2-small; batch size tuned for interactivity; prefix cache enabled for repeated prompts. For the distribution you shared (80% <300 tokens, 20% 300–2k tokens):
- Hosted: p95 ≈ 250–320 ms (steady), p99 ≈ 520–700 ms; during 250-concurrency spike p95 could rise ~20–40% without autoscaling.
- Dedicated (reserved with autoscale headroom): p95 ≈ 180–240 ms (steady), p99 ≈ 420–550 ms; spikes kept close to steady with autoscale and prewarmed workers.

3) Cost guidance (very rough, for modeling):
- Hosted: ~$3.10 per 1k tokens (baseline) — includes multi-tenant overhead, autoscale premium.
- Dedicated: ~$1.95 per 1k tokens (baseline) — amortized on reserved capacity; depends on utilization.

I'll prepare the one-page Tech Note and a short appendix with the detailed assumptions and a proposed sandbox start by Thu EOD (as Chloe requested). Also attaching a short SLA summary (redwood-sla-summary.pdf) and the draft RFI table we filled out.

Would you be available for a 30-minute calibration on Mon at 10am PT? We can walk the sandbox plan and finalize the RFI answers.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
